title: Morehouse College (Morehouse)
summary: Morehouse College (Morehouse) is a university in Atlanta. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with Morehouse.

sections.heading: What Morehouse is known for
paragraphs: Morehouse College (Morehouse) is a private nonprofit institution known for its strong emphasis on undergraduate education. With an enrollment of 2,844 students, Morehouse maintains a selective admission process, admitting approximately 44 percent of applicants. The college is particularly recognized for its business programs, which constitute about 36 percent of its academic offerings. Morehouse does not offer programs in the health field, focusing instead on disciplines that prepare students for leadership and professional success. As a private nonprofit college, Morehouse is dedicated to providing a rigorous and supportive educational environment.

sections.heading: How to read Morehouse tuition
paragraphs: Morehouse College (Morehouse) charges a tuition fee of $32,893 for both in-state and out-of-state students. This uniform tuition rate simplifies the cost structure for all attendees regardless of residency status. Beyond tuition, the total cost of attendance at Morehouse is estimated to be $51,433. This figure includes additional expenses such as fees, room and board, and other related costs necessary for a full academic year. Understanding these amounts provides a clearer picture of the financial commitment required to attend Morehouse.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Morehouse College (Morehouse) offers financial aid to a significant portion of its student body, with approximately 44.67% of students receiving Pell Grants. This federal aid is designed to assist students with demonstrated financial need. For those who complete their studies, the median debt incurred is about $25,000, reflecting the typical borrowing amount among graduates. Prospective and current students can explore detailed financial aid information and use the net price calculator available on Morehouse's official website at www.morehouse.edu/. Additional data on costs and financial aid can also be accessed through the College Scorecard at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?140553.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Career outcomes for Morehouse College (Morehouse) graduates reflect a moderate completion rate and earnings trajectory. Approximately 59.44 percent of students complete their programs within 150 percent of the expected time. The median earnings for graduates ten years after entry stand at $52,889, indicating the long-term financial benefits of a Morehouse education. Six years after entry, the median earnings are $38,267, showing early career income levels for completers. Among those who finish their studies, the median debt incurred is about $25,000, which provides context for the financial investment required to attain a degree from Morehouse. These figures collectively illustrate the economic outcomes associated with attending Morehouse College.

sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Morehouse College (Morehouse) is a historically Black men's college, reflected in its student body composition where 100 percent of students are men. The racial demographics show a predominant Black student population at approximately 97.26 percent, with very small representations of White, Hispanic, and Asian students, each constituting less than one percent. Morehouse's commitment to accessibility is also evident in its financial aid profile, with about 44.67 percent of students receiving Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of the student body comes from lower-income backgrounds.

sections.heading: Is Morehouse accredited?
paragraphs: Morehouse College is a private historically black men's liberal arts college located in Atlanta, Georgia. It is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award bachelor's degrees. This accreditation ensures that Morehouse meets established standards of quality and effectiveness in its educational programs and institutional operations.
